content: The National Health Workforce Accounts (NHWA) Implementation Guide is a comprehensive document developed by the World Health Organization (WHO) to support countries in systematically improving the availability, quality, and use of health workforce data. This guide is an essential tool for achieving universal health coverage, the United Nations Sustainable Development Goals, and other national and global health objectives. It is designed to assist countries in implementing the NHWA framework, which provides a standardized approach to collecting, monitoring, and reporting health workforce data. The guide emphasizes that countries may already have equivalent systems in place, such as human resources for health (HRH) registries or health workforce observatories, which can be adapted to align with the NHWA framework. The NHWA uses a labor market analysis framework to monitor key indicators that provide a comprehensive overview of the health workforce dynamics in a country. These indicators include data on health worker density, education, financing, migration, and more, as outlined in the ten modules of the WHO NHWA Handbook. The NHWA implementation process is divided into three phases: conceptualization, operationalization, and process revision and sustainability. Each phase includes specific steps to strengthen HRH data monitoring and reporting. These steps involve obtaining governmental commitment, establishing governance structures, conducting scoping and planning, developing a legal framework, compiling and analyzing data, validating findings, disseminating results, and revising processes for sustainability. Key principles of the guide include collaboration among stakeholders, integration with existing health information systems, and a do-no-harm approach to avoid unnecessary duplication or disruption of current systems. The guide is intended for policymakers, program managers, researchers, and other stakeholders involved in HRH policy, strategy, and data monitoring at national and international levels. It provides detailed recommendations and tools to help countries develop or improve their HRH information systems in a sustainable and standardized manner. The NHWA framework requires the establishment of a governance structure, including a multisectoral coordination working group, a secretariat for coordination and administration, a technical working group for data analysis, and a communications team to disseminate findings. The guide also outlines the importance of legal frameworks to govern data protection, confidentiality, and exchange. Regular reviews of the NHWA process are recommended to identify successes, address challenges, and incorporate new data sources and indicators. In summary, the NHWA Implementation Guide provides a structured approach for countries to enhance their health workforce data systems, enabling evidence-based decision-making and improved health system performance. It serves as a valuable resource for achieving sustainable and effective health workforce management.
